title: The scheme_eval Dispatch Function
description: A complete Scheme evaluator in one function that dispatches on expression type: atoms, symbols, special forms (quote, if, define, lambda, etc.), and procedure calls.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: SchemeError and Env are the same as Model 2: Env inherits from dict, stores outer, and find walks the chain for lexical lookup.

Procedure class represents a closure. __init__ captures params, body, and the defining env. __call__ creates a new call frame with outer=self.env (lexical scope), then evaluates the body in that frame.
scheme_eval starts with self-evaluating atoms: numbers, booleans return themselves. Strings starting with quote are string literals. Then symbols (plain strings) are looked up via env.find(x)[x].
If x is not a list or is empty, it's an error. head = x[0] is the first element. Special forms are checked by comparing head to keywords.

steps.question: The if special form at line 81 uses `test is not False` rather than `if not test`. Why is this exact check necessary in Scheme?
steps.answer: In Scheme, only #f (boolean false) is falsy. Zero, empty list, and empty string are all truthy. Using `if not test` would incorrectly treat 0 as false. The check `test is not False` implements Scheme's truthiness rule exactly.

steps.description: define has two forms. (define symbol value) evaluates value and binds it in the current env. (define (name params) body) desugars to (define name (lambda (params) body)) by creating a Procedure with the current env.
set! uses env.find(x[1]) to locate the frame where the variable is bound, then updates that frame. It can mutate outer bindings because it finds the actual frame holding the binding.
lambda creates a Procedure with params from x[1], body from x[2] (or wraps multiple expressions in begin), and captures the current env as the closure's defining environment.

let desugars to a lambda application: it extracts params and evaluates args in the current env. It creates a Procedure with those params and the body, then calls it with the evaluated args. This creates a new frame for the let bindings.

Procedure call: evaluate head to get the proc, evaluate all args, then if proc is callable, call proc(args). User-defined procedures are Procedure instances whose __call__ creates the call frame on the saved env.
Run it. make_global_env creates Env with primitives: +, -, *, /, comparison ops, not, display, newline as Python lambdas.
Tests loop begins. First: (+ 2 3) parses to ['+', 2, 3]. scheme_eval: head='+', looks up + in genv (primitive), evaluates args 2 and 3, calls primitive => 5. Prints => 5.
(if #t 42 0): test evaluates to True (not False), so branch is x[2]=42. scheme_eval(42, env) returns 42. Prints => 42.
(if #f 42 99): test is False, branch is x[3]=99. Evaluates to 99. Prints => 99.
(define x 10): binds x=10 in genv. Returns None, not printed.
(+ x 5): looks up + (primitive), looks up x=10, evaluates 5, calls + => 15. Prints => 15.
(define square (lambda (n) (* n n))): lambda creates Procedure(params=['n'], body=['*', 'n', 'n'], env=genv). define binds square to it in genv.
(square 7): looks up square (Procedure), evaluates 7, calls Procedure.__call__([7]): creates call_env with n=7, outer=genv, evaluates (* n n) => 49. Prints => 49.
